output.title: Weekly rhythm is a scope constraint, not a calendar note
output.body:
If you run a 1-10 person business, weekly rhythm is not just a scheduling detail. It is a design constraint. A workflow only makes sense for automation or AI if it fits into a repeatable slot in your week without forcing a new meeting, a new approval chain, or a hiring decision just to keep it alive.

The practical next step is to map one recurring task against your actual week. Write down when it happens, who has to touch it, and which step still needs human judgment. If the task shows up only once in a while, or if it depends on you reacting in the moment, that is useful information too. Not every problem deserves automation. Some deserve a better checklist, and that is fine.

If the task is regular enough, ask a narrower question: can one bounded step run inside the time you already have, with human approval kept for anything sensitive? That is the point where a pilot starts to look sensible. Keep the scope small, keep the decision human, and choose one concrete output you can inspect each week.

A good question to leave on your own whiteboard: what is the one repeating task that keeps showing up in the same part of your week, and is it actually ready for a process change?
